readings.title: The Brevity of Life
readings.subtitle: A resolve to guard the tongue gives way to a meditation on futility.
readings.text:
[Psalm 39:1] <dn>I</dn> have said,“Let me guard <dn>my</dn> ways Against sinning with <dn>my</dn> tongue; Let me guard <dn>my</dn> mouth with a muzzle, While the wrongdoer is before me.”
[2] <dn>I</dn> became dumb, keeping still; <dn>I</dn> was silent, from good; And <dn>my</dn> pain was stirred.
[3] <dn>My</dn> heart was hot within me; While <dn>I</dn> was meditating, the fire burned. Then <dn>I</dn> spoke with <dn>my</dn> tongue:
[4] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, let me know <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> end, And the measure of <dn>my</dn> days, what it is, Let me know how short-lived <dn>I</dn> am.
[5] “See, <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>my</dn> days as handbreadths, And <dn>my</dn> lifetime is as non-existence before <dn>You</dn>; Only, all men standing, are all breath. Selah.
[6] “As but a shadow each one walks; They busy themselves, only in vain; He heaps up wealth, But knows not who gathers them.

readings.title: A Plea for Deliverance
readings.subtitle: Hope is placed in YeHoVaH alone for deliverance from transgression and affliction.
readings.text:
[Psalm 39:7] “And now, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, what do <dn>I</dn> wait for? <dn>My</dn> expectancy is in <dn>You</dn>.
[8] “Deliver me from all <dn>my</dn> transgressions; Do not make me the reproach of the foolish.
[9] “<dn>I</dn> was dumb, <dn>I</dn> did not open <dn>my</dn> mouth, Because it was <dn>You</dn> who did it.
[10] “Turn aside <dn>Your</dn> stroke from me; <dn>I</dn> am overcome by the blow of <dn>Your</dn> hand.
[11] “When <dn>You</dn> chastise man for crookedness with reproofs, <dn>You</dn> consume <dn>את</dn> what he loves, like a moth; All men are but a breath. Selah.
[12] “Hear <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> prayer, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And give ear to <dn>my</dn> cry; Do not be silent at <dn>my</dn> tears; For <dn>I</dn> am a stranger with <dn>You</dn>, A sojourner, as all <dn>my</dn> fathers were.
[13] “Look away from me, That <dn>I</dn> might brighten up, Before <dn>I</dn> go away and am no more.”

readings.title: A New Song of Deliverance
readings.subtitle: Praise for being lifted from the pit of destruction.
readings.text:
[Psalm 40:1] <dn>I</dn> waited, waited for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; And <dn>He</dn> inclined to me, and heard <dn>my</dn> cry.
[2] And <dn>He</dn> drew me Out of the pit of destruction, Out of the muddy clay, And <dn>He</dn> set <dn>my</dn> feet upon a rock, <dn>He</dn> is establishing <dn>my</dn> steps.
[3] Then <dn>He</dn> put a new song in <dn>my</dn> mouth; Praise to our <dn>Elohim</dn>; Many do see it and fear, And trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[4] Blessed is that man who has made <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his trust, And has not turned to the proud, And those turning aside to falsehood.
[5] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, many are the wonders Which <dn>You</dn> have done, and <dn>Your</dn> purposes toward us; There is no one to compare with <dn>You</dn>; <dn>I</dn> declare and speak: They are too many to be numbered.

readings.title: Delight in Doing God's Will
readings.subtitle: Obedience from the heart is greater than sacrifice.
readings.text:
[Psalm 40:6] Slaughtering and meal offering <dn>You</dn> did not desire; <dn>You</dn> have opened <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> ears; Ascending offering and sin offering <dn>You</dn> did not ask for.
[7] Then <dn>I</dn> said, “See, <dn>I</dn> have come; In the scroll of the Book it is prescribed for me.
[8] <dn>I</dn> have delighted to do <dn>Your</dn> pleasure, O <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, And <dn>Your</dn> Torah is within <dn>my</dn> heart.”
[9] <dn>I</dn> have proclaimed <dn>את</dn> the good news of righteousness, In the great assembly; See, <dn>I</dn> do not restrain <dn>my</dn> lips, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> know.
[10] <dn>I</dn> did not conceal <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> righteousness within <dn>my</dn> heart; <dn>I</dn> have declared <dn>Your</dn> trustworthiness and <dn>Your</dn> deliverance; <dn>I</dn> did not hide <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment and <dn>Your</dn> truth From the great assembly.

readings.title: A Cry for Help
readings.subtitle: Overwhelmed by sins and enemies, the psalmist seeks swift deliverance.
readings.text:
[Psalm 40:11] Do not withhold <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> compassion from me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; Let <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment and <dn>Your</dn> truth always watch over me.
[12] For evils without number have surrounded me; <dn>My</dn> crookednesses have overtaken me, And <dn>I</dn> have been unable to see; They became more than the hairs of <dn>my</dn> head; And <dn>my</dn> heart has failed me.
[13] Be pleased, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to deliver me; O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, hasten to help me!
[14] Let those who seek to destroy <dn>my</dn> life Be ashamed and abashed altogether; Let those who are desiring <dn>my</dn> evil Be driven back and put to shame.
[15] Let those who say to me, “Aha, aha!” Be appalled at their own shame.
[16] Let all those who seek <dn>You</dn> Rejoice and be glad in <dn>You</dn>; Let those who love <dn>Your</dn> deliverance always say, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be exalted!”
[17] But <dn>I</dn> am poor and needy; Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> think upon me. <dn>You</dn> are <dn>my</dn> help and <dn>my</dn> deliverer; O <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not delay!

readings.title: The Blessedness of Considering the Poor
readings.subtitle: The psalmist laments the evil plots of his enemies during his sickness.
readings.text:
[Psalm 41:1] Blessed is he who considers the poor; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does deliver him in a day of evil.
[2] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does guard him and keep him alive; <dn>He</dn> is blessed on the earth, And <dn>You</dn> do not hand him over To the desire of his enemies.
[3] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sustains him on his sickbed; In his weakness on his bed <dn>You</dn> bring a change.
[4] As for me, <dn>I</dn> said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, show me favour; Heal <dn>את</dn> me, for <dn>I</dn> have sinned against <dn>You</dn>.”
[5] <dn>My</dn> enemies speak evil of me, “When he dies his name shall perish.”
[6] And when one comes to visit, he speaks falsely; His heart gathers wickedness to itself; He goes out, he speaks of it.
[7] All who hate me whisper together against me; They plot evil to me, saying,
[8] “A matter of Beliya‛al is poured out on him, That when he lies down, he would not rise again.”

readings.title: Betrayal by a Friend
readings.subtitle: A prayer for favor and restoration concludes with a doxology for Book One of Psalms.
readings.text:
[Psalm 41:9] Even <dn>my</dn> own friend in whom <dn>I</dn> trusted, who ate <dn>my</dn> bread, Has lifted up his heel against me.
[10] But <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, show me favour and raise me up, And let me repay them.
[11] By this <dn>I</dn> know that <dn>You</dn> did delight in me, Because <dn>my</dn> enemy does not shout for joy over me.
[12] And <dn>I</dn>, <dn>You</dn> uphold me in <dn>my</dn> integrity, And set me before <dn>Your</dn> face forever.
[13] Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl From everlasting to everlasting! Aměn and Aměn.

readings.title: The Corruption of Mankind
readings.subtitle: A declaration that the fool denies God, leading to universal depravity and judgment.
readings.text:
[Psalm 53:1] The fool has said in his heart, “There is no <dn>Elohim</dn>.” They have done corruptly, And they have done abominable unrighteousness; No one does good.
[2] <dn>Elohim</dn> looked down from the heavens on the children of men, To see if there is a wise one, seeking <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[3] They have all turned aside; They have together become filthy; No one is doing good, not even one.
[4] Have the workers of wickedness no knowledge, Who eat up <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> people as they eat bread, And do not call on <dn>Elohim</dn>?
[5] There they are in great fear, Where no fear was, For <dn>Elohim</dn> shall scatter <dn>את</dn> the bones Of him who encamps against you. You shall put them to shame, For <dn>Elohim</dn> has rejected them.
[6] O that <dn>את</dn> the deliverance of Yisra’ěl Would be given out of Tsiyon! When <dn>Elohim</dn> turns back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of <dn>His</dn> people, Let Ya‛aqoḇ rejoice, let Yisra’ěl be glad.

readings.title: A Cry of Anguish
readings.subtitle: The psalmist is overwhelmed by the enemy's oppression and longs to escape.
readings.text:
[Psalm 55:1] Give ear to <dn>my</dn> prayer, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, And do not hide <dn>Yourself</dn> from <dn>my</dn> plea.
[2] Give heed to me, and answer me; <dn>I</dn> wander and moan in <dn>my</dn> complaint,
[3] Because of the noise of the enemy, Because of the outcry of the wrong; For they bring down wickedness upon me, And in wrath they hate me.
[4] <dn>My</dn> heart is pained within me, And the frights of death have fallen upon me.
[5] Fear and trembling have come upon me, And shuddering covers me.
[6] And <dn>I</dn> said, “Who would give me wings like a dove! <dn>I</dn> would fly away and be at rest.
[7] “See, <dn>I</dn> would wander far off, <dn>I</dn> would lodge in the wilderness. Selah.
[8] “<dn>I</dn> would hasten <dn>my</dn> escape From the raging wind and storm.”

readings.title: The Sting of Betrayal
readings.subtitle: The deepest pain comes not from an enemy, but from a trusted companion.
readings.text:
[Psalm 55:9] Confuse, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, divide their tongues, For <dn>I</dn> saw violence and strife in the city.
[10] Day and night they go around it on its walls; Wickedness and trouble are also in the midst of it.
[11] Covetings are in its midst; Oppression and deceit do not vanish from its streets.
[12] It is not an enemy who reproaches me – That <dn>I</dn> could bear; Nor one who hates me who is making himself great against me – Then <dn>I</dn> could hide from him.
[13] But it was you, a man <dn>my</dn> equal, <dn>My</dn> companion and <dn>my</dn> friend.
[14] We took sweet counsel together, We walked to the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> in the throng.
[15] Let death come upon them; Let them go down into She’ol alive, For evil is in their dwellings, in their midst.

readings.title: Casting Burdens on YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: A confident appeal to God who saves, sustains, and brings the treacherous to ruin.
readings.text:
[Psalm 55:16] <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> call upon <dn>Elohim</dn>, And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saves me.
[17] Evening and morning and at noon <dn>I</dn> complain and moan, And <dn>He</dn> hears <dn>my</dn> voice.
[18] <dn>He</dn> has redeemed <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> life in peace From the battle against me, For there were many against me.
[19] <dn>Ěl</dn>, even <dn>He</dn> who sits enthroned from of old, Does hear and afflict them – Selah – Those with whom there are no changes, Those who do not fear <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[20] He has put forth his hands against those Who were at peace with him; He has broken <dn>את</dn> his covenant.
[21] His mouth was smoother than curds, Yet in his heart is fighting; His words were softer than oil, But they are drawn swords.
[22] Cast <dn>את</dn> your burden on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And let <dn>Him</dn> sustain you; <dn>He</dn> never allows the righteous to be shaken.
[23] For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, do bring them down To the pit of destruction; Men of blood and deceit do not reach half their days; But <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> trust in <dn>You</dn>.

readings.title: The Injustice of Wicked Rulers
readings.subtitle: The psalmist condemns the inherent corruption of those who should judge righteously.
readings.text:
[Psalm 58:1] Would you indeed speak righteousness, in silence? Do you judge straightly, you sons of men?
[2] No, in heart you work unrighteousness; On earth you weigh out <dn>את</dn> the violence of your hands.
[3] The wrong have been estranged from the womb; These who speak lies go astray from birth.
[4] Their poison is like the poison of a snake; Like a deaf cobra that stops its ear,
[5] So as not to hear the voice of whisperers, Or a skilled caster of spells.

readings.title: Imprecation Against the Wicked
readings.subtitle: A call for God to destroy the wicked, so the righteous will be vindicated.
readings.text:
[Psalm 58:6] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, break <dn>את</dn> their teeth in their mouth! Break out <dn>את</dn> the fangs of the young lions, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!
[7] Let them melt, let them vanish as water; Let <dn>Him</dn> aim <dn>His</dn> arrows that they be cut down;
[8] Like a snail which melts away as it moves, Like a woman’s stillbirth, Let them not see the sun!
[9] Before your pots feel the thorns, Whether green or ablaze, <dn>He</dn> sweeps them away.
[10] The righteous rejoices when he has seen <dn>את</dn> the vengeance, He washes his feet in the blood of the wrong,
[11] And man says, “Truly, the righteous are rewarded; Truly, there is an <dn>Elohim</dn> judging in the earth.”
